name: MindManager
tagline: Desktop mind mapping and visual outlining software with task data, templates, and Office export.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: A mind map is a tree drawn on a canvas, and a tree drawn on a canvas is one of the most tractable things you can ask a coding agent to build. The hard part is not the data model, it is the keyboard feel: Tab for child, Enter for sibling, instant re-layout, never touching the mouse. An agent can get that right in a session along with collapse, drag-to-reparent, PNG and Markdown export, and local file persistence. What you will not get is twenty years of desktop polish, the template library, task and Gantt metadata, or anything that round-trips into Word, PowerPoint, and Project. If you are one person dumping thoughts into a radial outline, none of that was the point.
coreLoopDIY: A local, keyboard-driven mind map editor that auto-layouts a node tree on an SVG canvas and exports to PNG, SVG, and Markdown.
requirements: Nothing else: runs fully local, no accounts, no cloud
whatYouLose: Office and Project integration, including the import and export round-trips that justify the license in corporate settings
Task metadata, resources, dependencies, and the Gantt views layered on top of the map
A very large template and style library plus decades of layout edge cases already solved
Multi-user sharing, co-editing, and published interactive HTML maps
Native desktop performance on maps with thousands of nodes
moatNotes: The moat is enterprise plumbing, not mind maps. Companies buy it because it drops output into Office and because it is the tool procurement already approved.
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay for MindManager because the map is rarely the deliverable. It gets turned into a slide deck, a project plan, or a document, and that handoff is the product. If your maps have to leave your head and land in someone else's PowerPoint with the formatting intact, a weekend build will quietly embarrass you. If maps are where your thinking lives and dies, the license is paying for integrations you never open.
notes: The classic one-shot: easy to build badly, and the difference between good and bad is entirely in the keyboard handling.
prompt:
Build a local-first mind mapping app. No accounts, no server, no telemetry, no cloud.

Stack: Vite + React + TypeScript. Zustand for state. SVG for rendering, no canvas library, no diagramming library. Plain CSS, no UI kit.

Data model: a single tree of nodes { id, text, children, collapsed, color }. Persist the whole document to localStorage on every change, debounced. Also support File System Access API save/open of a .mindmap.json file, with a download fallback.

Layout: implement a horizontal radial-ish tree layout yourself. Root in the center, children fan right and left alternating from the root's immediate children, descendants continue in their parent's direction. Compute subtree heights so siblings never overlap. Draw edges as cubic bezier curves from parent edge to child edge.

Keyboard first, this is the whole product:
- Tab: add child of selected node, enter edit mode
- Enter: add sibling below, enter edit mode
- F2 or double-click: edit text inline
- Escape: commit edit and return to navigation
- Arrow keys: move selection through the tree spatially
- Space: collapse/expand subtree
- Delete/Backspace on a selected non-editing node: delete subtree with confirm if it has children
- Cmd/Ctrl+Z and Shift+Cmd/Ctrl+Z: undo/redo, keep a 100-step history stack
Never require the mouse to build a map.

Mouse: drag a node onto another to reparent, drag empty space to pan, scroll to zoom, a fit-to-screen button.

Export: PNG (serialize the SVG to a canvas at 2x), raw SVG, and Markdown as a nested bullet list. Import: paste a nested Markdown bullet list and build the tree from indentation.

Out of scope, do not build: sharing, real-time collaboration, task or Gantt fields, Office export, templates, images in nodes, mobile layout.

Ship a README with run instructions and a keyboard shortcut table. Seed the app with a small example map on first load.
